lem-continuous-finite-variation-martinga:
## Statement

Let $D=(D_t)_{0\le t\le T}$ be a continuous martingale relative to a
filtration $(\mathcal F_t)$, with $D_0=0$. Suppose each path has finite total
variation $V_T(D)$ and $\mathbb E V_T(D)<\infty$. Then $D$ is indistinguishably
zero on $[0,T]$.
lem-bounded-stopping-preserves-cadlag-sq:
## Statement

Let $M=(M_t)_{0\le t\le T}$ be a square-integrable all-pairs martingale with
right-continuous paths with left limits for every $\omega$, and let $\tau\le T$
be a stopping time. Then the stopped process
$M^\tau_t:=M_{t\wedge\tau}$ is a square-integrable martingale on $[0,T]$.
def-counting-process-intensity-and-compe:
## Definition

Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]]. Fix a finite horizon
$T>0$, a probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal F,P)$ and a continuous-time
filtration $(\mathcal F_t)_{0\le t\le T}$ in the all-pairs convention of
[[def-continuous-time-filtration-and-all-pairs-martingale]]. A **simple
unit-jump counting process** is an adapted, càdlàg (right-continuous with left
limits), nondecreasing, integer-valued process $N$ with $N_0=0$,
$N_T<\infty$ almost surely, and $\Delta N_t\in\{0,1\}$ for every
$0<t\le T$ outside one null event; here $\Delta N_t:=N_t-N_{t-}$.

An **at-risk process** is a predictable process
$Y:[0,T]\times\Omega\to\{0,1\}$, and an **intensity density** is a finite,
nonnegative predictable process $\lambda$. Form the Lebesgue integral
$$A_t:=\int_0^tY_s\lambda_s\,ds,\qquad 0\le t\le T.$$
The **continuous intensity compensator contract** requires that this integral
be finite pathwise, that $A$ be continuous, adapted and predictable with
$A_0=0$, and that $\mathbb E[A_T]<\infty$. Set $M_t:=N_t-A_t$. The model
contract is the additional hypothesis that $M$ is a square-integrable
martingale relative to the stated filtration. Under this contract $A$ is a
continuous predictable compensator of $N$.

The displayed intensity density alone does **not** assert that $N-A$ is a
martingale, that such a process exists for a given $N$, or that the contract
follows from an empirical observation scheme. No general compensator-existence
theorem is included here. The Axiom of Choice is inherited from the
continuous-time martingale and conditional-expectation interfaces; no further
choice is used to state the model contract.
def-optional-and-predictable-brackets-fo:
## Definition

Work on the finite horizon $[0,T]$ of
[[def-counting-process-intensity-and-compensator-contract]]. For càdlàg
(right-continuous with left limits) finite-variation processes $X,Y$ starting
at zero, with $\Delta X_s:=X_s-X_{s-}$ and $\Delta Y_s:=Y_s-Y_{s-}$, define
their **optional quadratic covariation** by
$$[X,Y]_t:=\sum_{0<s\le t}\Delta X_s\,\Delta Y_s,$$
and write $[X]:=[X,X]$. The series is absolutely convergent because each path
has finite variation. This is the jump-sum convention for optional brackets
used on this page.

For a square-integrable model martingale $M=N-A$ from
[[def-counting-process-intensity-and-compensator-contract]], a **continuous
predictable bracket** $\langle M\rangle$ is a continuous, predictable,
increasing process $B$ with $B_0=0$, $\mathbb E[B_T]<\infty$, and $M^2-B$ a
martingale, when such a process exists. For two square-integrable model
martingales $M=N-A$ and $M'=N'-A'$ from that contract, a **continuous
predictable cross bracket** $\langle M,M'\rangle$ is a continuous, predictable
finite-variation process $C$ with $C_0=0$, $\mathbb E\operatorname{Var}(C)_T
<\infty$, and $[M,M']-C$ a martingale, when such a process exists. The
uniqueness lemma below fixes the meaning of “the” bracket in this continuous
compensator class. No general bracket-existence theorem is asserted.
The Axiom of Choice is inherited through the model martingale's
conditional-expectation interface; this definition makes no further choice.
def-elementary-predictable-counting-proc:
## Definition

Let $M$ be a square-integrable martingale on a finite horizon $[0,T]$ in the
all-pairs convention of
[[def-continuous-time-adapted-process-and-martingale]] (in particular, it may
be the compensated counting-process martingale of
[[def-counting-process-intensity-and-compensator-contract]]). Let
$$0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_m=T$$
be a deterministic partition, and let each bounded random variable $H_j$ be
$\mathcal F_{t_j}$-measurable. The associated **bounded predictable step
integrand** is $H_0=0$ at time $0$ and $H_s=H_j$ on $(t_j,t_{j+1}]$. For this
chosen step representation define, for $0\le t\le T$,
$$I_t(H):=\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}H_j\bigl(M_{t\wedge t_{j+1}}-M_{t\wedge t_j}\bigr).$$
This is a finite sum of square-integrable random variables. At this stage the
representation is part of the input; representation independence and the
isometry are established in
[[lem-elementary-counting-process-integral-isometry]].
The Axiom of Choice is inherited from the all-pairs martingale and
conditional-expectation interface; the finite-sum definition makes no
additional choice.
lem-predictable-step-processes-dense-in-:
## Statement

For the contract of
[[def-counting-process-intensity-and-compensator-contract]], let
$\mathcal P_T$ be the predictable sigma-algebra on $[0,T]\times\Omega$ and
define the finite measure
$$\mu(E):=\int_EY_s(\omega)\lambda_s(\omega)\,(ds\times P)(d(s,\omega)),\qquad E\in\mathcal P_T.$$
Then bounded predictable step processes are dense in $L^2(\mu)$. The time-zero
slice has $\mu$-measure zero.
def-l2-counting-process-integral:
## Definition

For the compensator contract on $[0,T]$, let $H$ be a predictable real
process with
$$\mathbb E\int_0^T H_s^2\,dA_s<\infty.$$
When the elementary integrals of a sequence of bounded predictable step
processes converging to $H$ in this norm converge in $L^2(P)$, denote the
resulting $L^2(P)$ class at time $t$ by
$$\int_0^t H_s\,dM_s.$$
The definition is conditional on existence of the limit. The L²-extension
theorem below proves existence for every such predictable $H$, independence
from the approximating sequence, the martingale property, and the isometry.
The Axiom of Choice is inherited through the conditional-expectation and
$L^2$-completion interfaces used by that theorem.
lem-continuous-predictable-bracket-uniqu:
## Statement

Let $X$ be an adapted process on $[0,T]$. Suppose $C,D$ are continuous,
predictable finite-variation processes with $C_0=D_0=0$,
$\mathbb E[\operatorname{Var}(C)_T+\operatorname{Var}(D)_T]<\infty$, and
both $X-C$ and $X-D$ are martingales. Then $C$ and $D$ are indistinguishable.
lem-elementary-counting-integral-preserv:
## Statement

Let $M$ be any square-integrable martingale on $[0,T]$, and let $H$ be a
bounded predictable step integrand on a deterministic partition. The elementary integral
$(I_t(H))_{0\le t\le T}$ of
[[def-elementary-predictable-counting-process-integral]] is a
square-integrable martingale.
lem-finite-variation-integration-by-part:
## Statement

Let $x:[0,T]\to\mathbb R$ be càdlàg (right-continuous with left limits) and of finite total variation. For any
deterministic partitions $\pi_n$ of $[0,T]$ with mesh tending to zero, and
each fixed $t\le T$, put $\Delta_j^n x(t)=x_{t\wedge t_{j+1}^n}-x_{t\wedge t_j^n}$.
Then
$$\sum_j(\Delta_j^n x(t))^2\longrightarrow [x]_t:=\sum_{0<s\le t}(\Delta x_s)^2,$$
and the left-endpoint sums satisfy
$$\sum_jx_{t\wedge t_j^n}\,\Delta_j^n x(t)\longrightarrow\frac{x_t^2-x_0^2-[x]_t}{2}.$$
thm-compensated-counting-process-bracket:
## Statement

Under the finite-horizon contract of
[[def-counting-process-intensity-and-compensator-contract]], the optional
quadratic variation of $M=N-A$ is $[M]_t=N_t$, its continuous predictable
bracket is $\langle M\rangle_t=A_t$, its self-cross predictable bracket is
$\langle M,M\rangle_t=A_t$, and $M_t^2-A_t$ is a martingale on $[0,T]$.
thm-cross-brackets-vanish-under-no-simul:
## Statement

Let $N^1,\ldots,N^k$ be simple unit-jump counting processes on one common
filtration, each satisfying the finite-horizon contract of
[[def-counting-process-intensity-and-compensator-contract]] with continuous
compensator $A^i$ and martingale $M^i=N^i-A^i$. If almost surely no two
distinct processes jump at the same time, then for $i\ne j$,
$$[M^i,M^j]_t=0\quad\text{and}\quad\langle M^i,M^j\rangle_t=0\qquad(0\le t\le T).$$
No independence assumption is required.
lem-elementary-counting-process-integral:
## Statement

Under the finite-horizon contract, for every bounded predictable step
integrand $H$, the elementary process $I_t(H)=\int_0^tH_s\,dM_s$ is a
square-integrable martingale and
$$\mathbb E[I_T(H)^2]=\mathbb E\int_0^TH_s^2\,dA_s.$$
The terminal $L^2$ class is independent of the chosen finite-step
representation of the same integrand in the compensator $L^2$ seminorm.
thm-l2-counting-process-integral-isometr:
## Statement

For every predictable $H$ on $[0,T]$ with
$\mathbb E\int_0^T H_s^2\,dA_s<\infty$, the limit in
[[def-l2-counting-process-integral]] exists at each $t\le T$, is independent
of the approximating step sequence, and defines a square-integrable
martingale. It satisfies, for each $t\le T$,
$$\mathbb E\left(\int_0^tH_s\,dM_s\right)^2=\mathbb E\int_0^tH_s^2\,dA_s.$$
